tx_lake_belton.blurb: Lake Belton is a reservoir near Temple, north of Austin, where steep limestone cliffs line the shore. Bouldering makes up most of the climbing, centered on Rogers Park: short walls of solid, pocketed rock that stay mostly in shade, with problems from easy up to roughly V11 and a generous share of beginner-to-intermediate grades. Sport climbing fills much of the rest, mainly at Miller Springs, where hard limestone on south and southwest facing walls rewards big moves between pockets, along with smaller crags such as Centex Sportsman Cave and Morgan's Point. Sport routes are short and steep, mostly 5.10 to 5.13 with the middle of that range best served. Trad and top-rope are rare.

wi_east_bluff_south.blurb: East Bluff South lies on the east side of Devil's Lake in the Baraboo Range, covering the ground between Mirror Talus and the Balanced Rock Trail. Nearly all of the climbing is bouldering, with problems from the easiest grades up to about V10, plus a smaller set of trad and top-rope lines from low to low-5.11 difficulty. Across the East Bluff, problems sit beside the lake below the bluff, among talus fields, and on small bands of cliff near the top. The park's rock is quartzite, attractive but slick, so edging works better than smearing. The largest clusters are around the Balanced Rock Trail, Mirror Talus, Birthday Talus and Horse Rampart Talus.

ca_el_cajon_mountain.blurb: El Cajon Mountain is a climbing destination in the eastern part of San Diego County, best known for sport climbing with a solid share of trad, a few aid lines and a small boulder. Routes run from single pitches to multi-pitch lines of several pitches. Grades cluster in the 5.10s, with plenty of 5.8 to 5.9 below and 5.11 to 5.12 above, and a few 5.13s at the top. Mountaineer Walls is the largest sector, followed by The Wedge, with Fly Dog Buttress and Quarry Wall much smaller. One crag within Mountaineer Walls is granite, mostly low-angle slab with mainly moderate lines; it faces south, so it is sunny and suits winter days, with a cooling breeze.

ma_hammond_pond.blurb: Hammond Pond is a small woodland reservation in Newton, west-southwest of Boston near Chestnut Hill. The rock is dark puddingstone conglomerate, broken into about a dozen small crags. Bouldering is the main draw, mostly V0 to V5 with a few harder problems, and the Alcove is known for its bouldering. A sizeable top-rope selection sits alongside it, easy to moderate and mostly 5.3 to 5.9, with a little trad. The Temple Area, the Alcove Area and a group of other walls and crags hold most of the climbs. It is a local's spot rather than a destination, and climbers who go without a rope should look carefully at the landings.

sd_palisades_state_park.blurb: Palisades State Park sits near Garretson in the prairie of eastern South Dakota, where Split Rock Creek has cut a gorge through pink Sioux quartzite. Spires and short cliffs rise straight from the water, so many climbs start right beside the creek. Trad and top-rope dominate, on crack systems, faces and roofs, and a dedicated bouldering area adds problems from V0 to about V5. Most roped routes fall between 5.6 and 5.10, with a smaller number of 5.11 and 5.12 lines. The rock offers little friction and a glassy feel, so crimps and slopers pump you out. Larger crags include South Wall, Hobgoblin's Hideout, Chockstone Tower and Harkor Tower. Spring, summer and fall suit it; summer is humid and buggy, and winter turns cold.

wa_bellingham_area.blurb: Bellingham Area gathers the climbing around Bellingham in northwest Washington, near the Canadian border and about ninety minutes up the interstate from Seattle. Bouldering makes up well over half of it, with problems from V0 to around V9, mostly easy to middle grades. Sport, trad and top-rope routes fill in the rest, mostly 5.9 to 5.11 with a few harder. Larrabee is the biggest sector, spread along the ocean and holding boulders plus some top-rope and trad; tides matter for the seaside walls. Sehome Arboretum is also boulder-heavy. Julia's Outcrop and The Burnout are mainly sport, and Squire Ridge offers top-rope climbing.
